full_judgment:
7. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptor-petitioner submits that the Revisional Court below under misconception of law and facts allowed the application for local investigation in a pre-emption case being summary proceeding in which there is no legal scope to decide title and possession of the parties and as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 7-7-2010 is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that the lower Revisional Court ought to have held that it is not necessary to investigate the RS and BS Plots of the impugned kabala along with other documents for disposal of the pre-emption proceedings but the Court below without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally by the impugned order allowed the application for local investigation after setting-aside the well founded order of the trial Court below and, as such, the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate finally submits that the proceeding initiated under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is a summary one, such summary proceeding demanded expeditious disposal of the application for preemption without entering into any complicated question of law or technicalities and neither can the Court be expected to enter into the investigation regarding the title of the land under pre-emption in the entire land covered by the kabala. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the petitioner to fortify his argument has relied on the decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 334, 5 BLD (AD) 183 and 55 DLR 149. 

 12. I have already noticed that the proceeding initiated under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in which the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 after filing written objection filed an application for local investigation to ascertain the true position of RS dag corresponding to CS and BS dag of the case land. It appears that pre-emptee-opposite party filed written statement denying most of the allegation of the pre-emption application stating, inter-alia, that the pre-emption case is not maintainable inasmuch as, the pre-emptee-opposite party did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land under pre-emption pursuant to the impugned kabala No.2764 dated 13-8-2000.
